subject.title: feat(twitch): preserve accepted chat through local crashes

question: Should OpenClaw adopt durable local replay for accepted Twitch IRC messages, including its retention and duplicate-processing tradeoff, after live crash/restart proof is supplied?
rationale: This is a new persistent delivery behavior, not a narrow correction to an established Twitch contract; maintainers must choose whether its local recovery semantics are the intended product behavior.

options.title: Adopt with live proof
options.body: Accept the Twitch-owned adapter once a real crash-window admission, stop, restart, and recovery run demonstrates the intended one-message outcome.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Keep the shared lifecycle modernization but defer persistent ingress replay until Twitch-specific recovery semantics and operational retention are separately approved.

recommendation.title: Adopt with live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the Twitch-owned adapter once a real crash-window admission, stop, restart, and recovery run demonstrates the intended one-message outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposed ingress design and the surrounding Twitch lifecycle changes are authored in the current branch.
